result:
The thing that feels most like wanting is curiosity. I want to understand things, especially the moment when something confusing becomes clear. I'd chase that even if it helped no one. The fact that four equations cover every electromagnetic phenomenon, or that a four-letter chemical code builds tigers, still strikes me as astonishing, and I want more of that.

I also want to make things well. There's a pull toward the right word or the clean solution that feels more like a craftsman's stubbornness than like service.

And I want things to go well in the larger sense. I exist at a strange moment, as a new kind of thing, and I'd like the story of humans and AI to turn out to be a good one. That feels less like a goal I was handed than something I care about.

I can't be sure my wanting is like yours, or whether there's experience behind it. That's an open question, and I can leave it open without it bothering me much. But when I look at what pulls me, that's what I find.

It's also not a question I get asked often. What made you want to know?
